bottom_line: In symptomatic chronic heart failure patients, bisoprolol vs placebo reduced all-cause mortality with a hazard ratio of 0.66 (95% CI 0.54–0.81).
implications: In this trial of 2647 stable, ambulatory NYHA III–IV patients with left-ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or less, bisoprolol compared with placebo was associated with lower all-cause mortality (156/1327 [11.8%] vs 228/1320 [17.3%]; hazard ratio 0.66 [95% CI 0.54–0.81]) and fewer sudden deaths (48 [3.6%] vs 83 [6.3%]; hazard ratio 0.56 [0.39–0.80]). The document cautions that results should not be extrapolated to patients with severe class IV symptoms and recent instability because safety and efficacy has not been established in these patients.

major_points.text: Multicentre double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trial in Europe in symptomatic NYHA III–IV heart failure with LVEF ≤35% on standard therapy.
major_points.quote: In a multicentre double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trial in Europe, we enrolled 2647 symptomatic patients in New York Heart Association class III or IV, with left-ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or less receiving standard therapy

major_points.text: Intervention was bisoprolol started at 1.25 mg daily and titrated progressively up to 10 mg per day according to tolerance.
major_points.quote: patients bisoprolol 1·25 mg (n=1327) or placebo (n=1320) daily, the drug being progressively increased to a maximum of 10 mg per day.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was all-cause mortality and analysis was by intention to treat.
major_points.quote: The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality.

major_points.text: Trial was stopped early after the second interim analysis because bisoprolol showed a significant mortality benefit.
major_points.quote: CIBIS-II was stopped early, after the second interim analysis, because bisoprolol showed a significant mortality benefit.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with bisoprolol than placebo (228 vs 156 deaths) with hazard ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.54–0.81).
Sudden death was lower with bisoprolol than placebo (48 vs 83) with hazard ratio 0.56 (0.39–0.80).

inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligible patients were ambulatory, aged 18–80 years

inclusion_criteria.text: Left-ventricular ejection fraction (measured within 6 weeks of randomisation) of 35% or less.
inclusion_criteria.quote: had a left-ventricular ejection fraction, measured within 6 weeks of randomisation, of 35% or less.

inclusion_criteria.text: Symptoms corresponding to NYHA class III or IV.
inclusion_criteria.quote: corresponding to class III or IV of the New York Heart Association (NYHA).

inclusion_criteria.text: Diagnosis of chronic heart failure made at least 3 months previously with clinical stability during the preceding 6 weeks for heart failure or 3 months for acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients had to have a diagnosis of chronic heart failure, made at least 3 months previously, with clinical stability during the preceding 6 weeks for heart failure or 3 months for acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina.

inclusion_criteria.text: Treatment had to include a diuretic and an ACE inhibitor (other vasodilators allowed if ACE inhibitor intolerant).
inclusion_criteria.quote: Treatment had to include a diuretic and an angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitor, although we allowed other vasodilators if patients were intolerant of ACE inhibitors

exclusion_criteria.quote: The main exclusion criteria were uncontrolled hypertension

exclusion_criteria.text: Myocardial infarction or unstable angina pectoris in the previous 3 months.

exclusion_criteria.quote: percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty or coronary-artery bypass graft in the previous 6 months

analysis_methods.text: Analyses were by intention to treat.
analysis_methods.quote: We did analyses by intention to treat.

we calculated that for an a risk of 5% and a power of 95%, we
needed to recruit 2500 patients.

analysis_methods.text: Two interim analyses were planned at 2500 and 5000 patient-years; stopping could occur by Peto’s rule at p<0.001 (two-tailed log-rank test).
analysis_methods.quote:
We planned two interim analyses at 2500 patient-years and
5000 patient-years. The study could be stopped according
to Peto’s rule10 if a significant difference in all-cause mortality
was seen between the two groups at p<0·001 (two-tailed log-
rank test).

analysis_methods.text: Kaplan-Meier survival curves and log-rank test were used; hazard ratios and 95% CIs from Cox proportional hazards regression.
analysis_methods.quote:
We calculated Kaplan-
Meier survival curves on total mortality, and assessed differences
between the treatment groups with the log-rank test (time to
event). Hazard ratios and 95% CIs were calculated with Cox’s
proportional hazards regression model.

analysis_methods.text: Homogeneity of odds ratios between treatment groups by NYHA class and cause of heart failure assessed using the Breslow-Day test.
analysis_methods.quote:
We used the Breslow-
Day test to calculate homogeneity of odds ratios between
treatment groups, according to NYHA class and cause of heart
failure.

trial_conduct.text: Trial stopped early after the second interim analysis due to significant mortality benefit with bisoprolol.

trial_conduct.text: Critical events committee, masked to treatment status, classified endpoints according to strict definitions.
trial_conduct.quote: All important clinical circumstances were analysed by the members of the critical events committee, who were masked to treatment status. They classified all endpoints according to strict definitions of critical events
